messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High memory in redwood-serving pool-7 (node=rtx-7c). Container crash loops + CUDA OOMs detected in paged-attn allocator. 5 node flaps in last 20m. Affected: kv-cache/paged-attn. Please ack and triage.

oncall-alyssa: Ack. I'm seeing a spike of 5xx on /v1/generate for models using kv-paged. p95 latency 1.8s -> 4.5s, 5xx ~12% over last 15m. Some Dedicated tenants reporting partial outputs. Will take lead. :rotating_light:

eng-kai: grabbing logs and core dumps now. Initial hunch: slow fragmentation (reservoir/porosity) in KV allocator causing slow OOM creep and eventual container crash. Mitigation proposal: 1) disable KV prefetch/cache on pool-7, 2) reduce max_batch_tokens -> 512, 3) route high-load traffic to fallback quantized model variant. I can push hotfix.

sre-lina: Can we cordon the node to stop new pods landing? I'll do that and start controlled drain.

oncall-alyssa: cordon command run: `kubectl cordon rtx-7c` — not draining yet (want to keep pods for immediate in-place triage).

eng-kai: dropping a brief error excerpt from node logs:
```
E 2024-06-01T12:44:02Z redwood-serving[pid:4231]: CUDA ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
W 2024-06-01T12:44:03Z allocator: paged-attn: slab alloc failed at 0x7fffbadf... returning -ENOMEM
kv_cache: resident_pages=3.1G total_alloc=10.8G free_fragments=8% evict_queue_len=0
```

eng-kai: note the evict_queue_len=0 despite memory pressure — looks like an eviction race where the compaction/evict loop isn't progressing. This explains slow creep over ~18h.

support-jordan: Customer ops: two paying customers opened tickets about latency and truncated outputs, third reported 502s. Ops is notifying them; sending initial incident note.

pm-maya: Pls include ETA + whether there's risk of logs/state loss for customers.

eng-kai: ETA for hotfix + rolling restart ~30-45m. No customer data loss expected — KV cache is ephemeral. Warming will take time; we'll serve from fallback model while caches warm.

oncall-alyssa: Executing staged mitigation now: 1) disable prefetch on pool-7 (`REDWOOD_KV_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1` via patch), 2) lower batching (max_batch_tokens=512), 3) trigger runtime compaction: `/opt/redwood/bin/realtime ctl kv compact --pool pool-7 --force`. Running compaction now.

incident-bot: ACTION STARTED: kv compact job id=0xabc123 for pool-7.

sre-lina: kicked rolling restart of redwood-serving pods in pool-7 (maxUnavailable=1). Also updated routing policy to send new sessions to fallback model-quant-2 for the heavy routes.

oncall-alyssa: monitoring: p95 dropping -> 2.1s, 5xx -> 3% after initial changes. Memory usage on problem nodes starting to trend down (observed ~1.2G reclaimed so far). :thumbsup:

eng-kai: compaction completed, reclaimed ~1.8G fragmented pages. Dumped heap profile and attached to internal ticket. Patch drafted to fix eviction race + ensure evict_queue progress under high contention.

support-jordan: Notified affected customers: update sent (ETA 45m, mitigation in progress, no data loss).

oncall-alyssa: Handing off watch to @eng-kai for the remainder of the night. Summary: hotfix applied (prefetch disabled + batch down), compaction done, rolling restarts in flight, routing to fallback applied, customer notifications sent. Warmup expected 30m. If anything regresses escalate to @sre-lina.

eng-kai: Ack — I'll own night watch until 02:00 UTC. Will open follow-up bug with reproducer, heap profiles, and suggested runtime fix (evict loop robustness). Will also schedule a small performance test to validate fallback routing behavior.

oncall-alyssa: Great work team — closing the active alert here but keeping the thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
